The man crowned Roman Emperor in AD 800 was **Charlemagne** (Charles the Great), who was proclaimed "Emperor of the Romans" by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day, December 25, 800.

The last name **Sylvester** comes from the Latin name *Silvester* or *Sylvester*, derived from the Latin adjective *silvestris* (meaning "wooded" or "of the forest") from *silva* ("wood" or "forest").

During the era of Charlemagne (early Middle Ages, around year 800 AD), the form of this Latin language was known as **Medieval Latin**. This was the form of Literary Latin used in Roman Catholic Western Europe during the Middle Ages. It served as the administrative, religious, and scholarly language throughout Charlemagne's realm and across medieval Europe, even though spoken languages were rapidly diverging into what would become modern Romance and Germanic languages.
